newsitem.title: FINLAND: UN's Rehn says human rights key for Bosnia vote.
newsitem.headline: UN's Rehn says human rights key for Bosnia vote.

text.p: Elisabeth Rehn, the United Nations human rights investigator for former Yugoslavia, said on Monday local elections in Bosnia should be postponed if human rights conditions are not met.

"I think it is more important that the human rights conditions for holding elections be met than it is (to know) when they will be held," Rehn told a news conference following a visit last week to Bosnia, Kosovo and Eastern Slavonia.
"The elections may have to be delayed, in which case they would have to be pushed back a long way," Rehn said referring to plans for a municipal ballot in Bosnia on November 23 and 24.

"The big question...is how well the sixth and seventh articles of the Dayton agreement have been fulfilled -- that is, the conditions on the return of refugees and displaced persons and on human rights," Rehn said.

Rehn, a former Finnish defence minister, added her voice to diplomats who have said international organisers need more time to correct problems which appeared in the September 14 vote for national offices in Bosnia.

She said she had discussed the issue with Carl Bildt, the international high representative to Bosnia, and Robert Frowick, the American head of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe's (OSCE) mission in Bosnia.
Rehn said Frowick was pushing strongly for holding the elections. Bildt, though apprehensive, was prepared to see them go ahead if the human rights situation was satisfactory.
"But it is clear the situation is not satisfactory," Rehn said. Displaced people's efforts to return to their homes were still "in real trouble."
The OSCE, which is supervising the local elections, has been criticised by opposition parties and independent analysts for its handling of the September national poll.

Critics have said the OSCE failed to account for an extraordinarily high voter turnout and shied away from punishing violations of the Dayton peace accord, which required the vote be held under "free and fair" conditions.
Rehn said the international community had decided to look the other way on human rights in order to enable Bosnia to hold the nationwide elections, but this should not happen again.
"Last time we looked through out fingers," she said. "It shouldn't happen a second time."
